html:
This map territory near Anadarko in southwestern Oklahoma is land shared by three tribes: the Wichita and Affiliated Tribes, the Caddo Nation and the Delaware Nation. It is shown on the 1492 map, but the three only came together here in the 1850s and 1860s.

The Wichita were farmers of the southern plains whose towns Spanish explorers visited in 1541. The Caddo came from the Red River country of Louisiana and east Texas, and the Delaware Nation is a western branch of the Lenape, pushed from the Atlantic coast step by step over two centuries. The US placed them on a reservation here in Indian Territory in 1859, and in 1901 broke it up into private plots and opened the rest to settlers. The Kiowa, Comanche and Apache lands lie next to it.
